Rhododendron ( / ˌ r oʊ d ə ˈ d ɛ n d r ən / ; pl. : rhododendra ), from Ancient Greek ῥόδον ( rhódon ), meaning "rose", and δένδρον ( déndron ), meaning "tree", [ 5 ] [ 6 ] [ 7 ] is a very large genus of about 1,024 species of woody plants in the heath family (Ericaceae). They can be either evergreen or deciduous . Most species are native to eastern Asia and the Himalayan region, but smaller numbers occur elsewhere in Asia , and in North America , Europe and Australia . [ 8 ]
